A two-time [[Minnesota State High School League]] (MSHSL) champion, White was named a Class 3A MSHSL champion in 2006 as a freshman at [[DeLaSalle High School]]; as a senior, he was named [[Minnesota Mr. Basketball]] and won a H Class 4A MSHSL championship with [[Hopkins High School]] in 2009, leading Hopkins to a perfect (31–0) record. White played [[college basketball]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball|Iowa State Cyclones]], leading the [[2011–12 Iowa State Cyclones men's basketball team|2011–12 team]] in every major statistical category. White was selected by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the first round of the [[2012 NBA draft]]. While White did not play for the Rockets, he played in three games for the [[Sacramento Kings]] in 2014. He gained notoriety for his [[generalized anxiety disorder]] (GAD), mainly triggered by a fear of flying, which led to disagreements with the Rockets over mental health issues and travel.{{Cite news |first=Dan |last=Devine |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/royce-white-skeptical-nba-genuinely-cares-players-mental-health-155413843.html |title=Why Royce White is skeptical the NBA genuinely cares about players' mental health |work=[[Yahoo! From 2016 to 2018, White played for the [[London Lightning]] of the [[National Basketball League of Canada|NBL Canada]], winning an NBL Canada championship and an [[Most valuable player|MVP]] award. After initially leading several [[Black Lives Matter]] protests in 2020,{{cite web |last1=Young |first1=Ryan |title=Ex-NBA player Royce White leads massive peaceful protest down Minneapolis interstate after George Floyd's death |url=https://www.yahoo.com/now/nba-iowa-state-royce-white-leads-peaceful-protest-minneapolice-interstate-george-floyd-death-police-005026776.html |website=Yahoo News |date=May 30, 2020 |access-date=August 30, 2021 |archive-date=August 30, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830024725/https://www.yahoo.com/now/nba-iowa-state-royce-white-leads-peaceful-protest-minneapolice-interstate-george-floyd-death-police-005026776.html |url-status=live}} White would enter politics in 2022. He ran an unsuccessful campaign in the Republican primary for [[Minnesota's 5th congressional district]] as a [[right-wing politics|right-wing]] [[Populism|populist]]. In 2024 White ran as the party's nominee for the [[U.S. Senate]], losing to incumbent [[Amy Klobuchar]]. Two years later, he unsuccessfully sought the party's U.S. Senate nomination once more in [[2026 United States Senate election in Minnesota #Republican party|2026]], this time finishing third place. His campaigns have been noted for their embrace of conspiracy theories.{{cite news |last1=Wendling |first1=Mike |title=Royce White: A candidate's controversial path from NBA to Maga |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c20r412qeydo |access-date=1 October 2024 |work=BBC News |date=14 August 2024 |archive-date=November 11, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241111150241/https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c20r412qeydo |url-status=live }}{{Cite news |date=2022-04-28 |title=How a former NBA player and activist became a far-right media darling |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/04/28/royce-white-nba-minnesota-congress/ |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20221217211913/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2022/04/28/royce-white-nba-minnesota-congress/ |archive-date=2022-12-17 |access-date=2026-09-07 |work=Washington Post |language=en}}{{Cite web | title=Royce White wins Republican nomination for U.S. Senate to face off against Sen. Amy Klobuchar - CBS Minnesota | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/minnesota/news/royce-white-republican-nomination-us-senate/ | access-date=2026-09-06 | website=www.cbsnews.com}} == Early life == White was born on April 10, 1991, in Minneapolis, the son of Kevin Tucker and Rebecca White. He is of [[Multiracial Americans|multiracial origin]], with Mexican, [[Norwegians|Norwegian]], [[Welsh people|Welsh]], and African-American ancestry.{{Cite web |title=How the NBA Failed Royce White |work=Longreads |date=August 2017 |access-date=November 25, 2021 |url=https://longreads.com/2017/08/31/how-the-nba-failed-royce-white/ |archive-date=November 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125210640/https://longreads.com/2017/08/31/how-the-nba-failed-royce-white/ |url-status=live}} White's grandfather, Frank White, is a Minnesotan baseball historian, and his great-grandfather, Louis "Pud" White Jr., was a baseball player in [[Negro league baseball|Negro]] and semi-professional leagues.{{cite web |last1=Dalla Costa |first1=Morris |title=London Lightning's Royce White is an athlete and philosopher who left NBA |url=https://lfpress.com/2017/03/03/london-lightnings-royce-white-is-an-athlete-and-philosopher-who-left-nba |website=The London Free Press |access-date=August 11, 2026 |date=March 3, 2017}} His uncle, [[Dave Winfield]], was a professional baseball player. White's father was not present in his life when he was young; they reconnected when White was 13. He witnessed his mother be mistreated by an abusive boyfriend.{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=For Royce White, it's a matter of trust |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8462144/nba-houston-rockets-royce-white-bus-request-matter-trust |website=ESPN |access-date=August 11, 2026 |date=October 5, 2012}} White split time living with his mother, his grandfather and other relatives in different areas of [[Minneapolis–Saint Paul]]. He was first diagnosed with mental health issues aged 16 when he had a "massive panic attack" after smoking marijuana. == High school basketball career == White went to [[DeLaSalle High School (Minneapolis)|DeLaSalle High School]] for his freshman, sophomore, and junior years.{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/preps/11651761.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203040200/http://www.startribune.com/sports/preps/11651761.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 3, 2013|title=3A: Duluth East, DeLaSalle to meet in title game|access-date=December 3, 2011|date=March 23, 2006|work=[[Star Tribune]]|author=Schmid, Pam}} The team won a state championship in 2006.{{Cite web|url=https://patch.com/minnesota/hopkins/hopkins-grad-royce-white-goes-no-16-in-nba-draft|title=Hopkins Grad Royce White Goes No. 16 in NBA Draft|date=June 29, 2012|website=Hopkins, MN Patch|access-date=September 5, 2023|archive-date=September 5, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230905123833/https://patch.com/minnesota/hopkins/hopkins-grad-royce-white-goes-no-16-in-nba-draft|url-status=live}} Following his sophomore season, in which he led DeLaSalle to a 19–8 record, White participated in the 2007 LeBron James US Skills Academy in [[Akron, Ohio]] and The [[Nike Global Challenge]] at the [[University of Portland]].
